connection.note: Painted during Van Gogh’s stay at Saint-Paul-de-Mausole. The landscape combines observation and imagination. Town-level pin. The hospital is documented; this marker is not its precise address.

One of the sunflower canvases made in Arles. This record represents the 1888 National Gallery painting, NG3863; the other versions remain separate works. Town-level pin; no exact studio coordinates asserted.

The first painted version of Van Gogh’s bedroom in the Yellow House. The later versions were made in 1889 and are different objects. Town-level pin; the depicted room and the act of painting are distinct facts.

The story began during Shelley’s summer near Geneva. This pin marks its beginning; the novel was developed and completed later in England. Lake Geneva area. No claim that the entire novel was written here.
connection.sourceLabel: Mary Shelley · Author’s introduction and 1818 edition

connection.note: The first edition appeared anonymously in London in three volumes. Publication is a separate connection from the places where the novel was written. City-level publication location; not the author’s residence.

Hugo resumed the novel during his exile on Guernsey. Its composition spans several places and periods; he had begun it in Paris in 1845. Saint Peter Port town-level pin; this is one writing location, not the entire composition history.

A first edition was published in Brussels by A. Lacroix, Verboeckhoven et Cie. There was also a Paris original edition; Brussels is not the only publication place. City-level publisher location. Parallel original editions remain distinct.

The Crystal Palace in Hyde Park hosted an international exhibition of manufacturing and design. Included as a historical event, not as a painting-only exhibition. Hyde Park is documented; the map uses a London city pin.
connection.sourceLabel: Victoria and Albert Museum · Great Exhibition

connection.note: Van Gogh was born in the Dutch village of Zundert. Town / city-level pin. Selected chapter; intervening journeys and residences are omitted.
The young Vincent worked for the art dealers Goupil & Cie in The Hague. Town / city-level pin. Selected chapter; intervening journeys and residences are omitted.

Work for Goupil brought Van Gogh to London. This is a selected life chapter, not a claim of uninterrupted residence. Town / city-level pin. Selected chapter; intervening journeys and residences are omitted.
Van Gogh lived and worked in Nuenen, developing paintings of rural life. Town / city-level pin. Selected chapter; intervening journeys and residences are omitted.
Van Gogh moved to Antwerp before continuing to Paris. Town / city-level pin. Selected chapter; intervening journeys and residences are omitted.
In Paris, Van Gogh encountered new approaches to colour and painting. Town / city-level pin. Selected chapter; intervening journeys and residences are omitted.
In Arles, he painted the Sunflowers and the first version of The Bedroom. Town / city-level pin. Selected chapter; intervening journeys and residences are omitted.
During his stay at Saint-Paul-de-Mausole, Van Gogh continued to paint, including The Starry Night. Town / city-level pin. Selected chapter; intervening journeys and residences are omitted.
Van Gogh spent his last months in Auvers-sur-Oise, making paintings of the village and surrounding fields. Town / city-level pin. Selected chapter; intervening journeys and residences are omitted.
Van Gogh died in Auvers-sur-Oise on 29 July 1890. Town / city-level pin. Selected chapter; intervening journeys and residences are omitted.
